newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait freezes British Aerospace deal - paper.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait freezes British Aerospace deal - paper.

text.p: Kuwait, bowing to parliamentary pressure, has put on hold a missile deal with British Aerospace Plc, a newspaper reported on Sunday.
"The government stopped measures to conclude an arms deal (Sea Skua missiles) for the Kuwait Navy," al-Qabas daily said.
Last week industry experts told Reuters that Kuwait was finalising the missile deal despite a demand by parliament to further probe the contract.
The missiles will arm Kuwait's eight, French-made $500 million fast patrol boats ordered in 1995. The first of the 42- metre vessels was finished last month.

The daily said Kuwaiti MPs later held contacts with senior officials to stop the deal. The government has not commented on the issue in recent weeks but last month it told parliament the decision to buy the British missiles was final.

Nasser al-Sanea, head of parliament's finance committee, said fellow MPs launched a drive "to prevent the conclusion of the deal," Qabas said. "The government cannot ignore legal measures ... represented by parliament's recommendations."
The previous parliament in 1996 asked its Public Funds Protection Committee to probe the deal after a cheaper offer for France's Aerospatiale MM-15 missile was dropped.

Kuwait newspapers have earlier said the British offer was for around $90 million but experts said the contract was split into several deals, including training and a British gift of 20 Sea Skua missiles, making it difficult to give an exact figure.
